solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: East of Cork, perhaps, a mean house

indicators.note: in an across entry the east side is the right, so the following letters sit after the stopper

parts.note: a cork is one example of a bung, a stopper for a bottle or barrel
low means mean or base, as in a low trick

explanation.surface: A cheap, shabby house somewhere to the east of the Irish city of Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city, so 'East of Cork' reads as a place; in fact it says A LOW comes to the right of BUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-storey dwelling is one particular kind of house.

clue.text: Does sensible thing as driver and stops talking

definitions.meaning: a careful motorist fastens the seat restraint before setting off
an informal phrase for falling silent, telling someone to shut up

explanation.surface: A careful motorist buckles in and goes quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb literally means fastening a seat restraint and, as slang, means to hush.

clue.text: Ultimately son, you fear, is like sister?

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so the closing letter of each of the five words is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a boy is behaving like his sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' is a sibling in the surface; in Britain a sister is also a senior hospital ward nurse, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior female member of the ward's medical care staff.

clue.text: Churchmen bow twice, awfully posh

parts.note: an arch is a bow shape, a curve
bis is Latin for twice, used on a score to mean repeat

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of posh are jumbled

explanation.surface: Churchmen bow repeatedly in a very grand manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges POSH into HOPS. BIS, meaning twice, is the musical instruction to repeat a passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior bishops heading a province of the church are clergy, i.e. churchmen.

clue.text: Oxford University sent up Disney's Robin Hood?

indicators.note: in a down entry, sent up means the word is written bottom to top, reading backwards

parts.note: Walt was the first name of the animator Disney

explanation.surface: Oxford mocks the Disney cartoon version of Robin Hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' looks like mockery, but it turns WALT into TLAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the archetypal English bandit living beyond the reach of the courts.

clue.text: Bachelor unwell, finding invoice

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A sick single man receives a demand for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of money owed for goods or services is a synonym for an invoice.

clue.text: Popular books about voting system — one still being published?

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pair of pieces wraps round the second

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
PR is proportional representation, an electoral system
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Popular books discussing an electoral system remain on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the first pair round the second, so PRI lands between the two halves of the Popular-plus-books string.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that is still available from its publisher has not gone out of stock for good.

clue.text: Dreary, ugly? Oddly, on reflection, was attractive

definitions.note: a phrase meaning drew in or tempted, matching a past-tense verb

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things reversed, so the picked letters run backwards
oddly means the first, third, fifth and further odd-numbered letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone dull and plain-looking somehow, looking back, held real appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' picks D, E, R, U, L from 'Dreary, ugly'; 'on reflection' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: To have enticed or tempted someone is to have drawn them in.

clue.text: Part of song Cyril botched

indicators.note: botched means bungled, so the name's letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Cyril made a mess of a section of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of a song, or one line of them, form a part of it.

clue.text: Snarer of wildlife returning in salesman role

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: rep is short for representative, a travelling salesman
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: A hunter going back to playing a travelling salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who catches animals in snares, often for fur, catches wildlife.

clue.text: Awfully dark news was embarrassment

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Terrible gloomy news caused shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment and social discomfort are near synonyms.

clue.text: She's back in the USSR

definitions.note: a woman's name, so the clue's she is the person meant

indicators.note: back means the found letters are read in reverse
in means the letters are found inside the words the USSR

explanation.surface: A woman has returned to the Soviet Union, echoing a Beatles song title.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Beatles' 'Back in the USSR'. 'in' finds EUS in 'the USSR' and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, shortened from Susan, stands for a woman.

clue.text: Very unpromising offer to accept right winger

parts.note: a black outlook is a very gloomy, unpromising one

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the offer holds the letter for right

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction

explanation.surface: A dismal offer is made to sign a right-sided wing player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right winger' suggests a footballer or politician; 'winger' alone is the definition, a creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A common songbird is a winged creature, i.e. a winger in crossword terms.

clue.text: Becomes strained when speaking a few words

indicators.note: when speaking means the word is said aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: tempers or nerves fray when they become strained

explanation.surface: Someone's voice goes tense whenever they talk briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A short group of words forming a unit of expression.

clue.text: Fall back on large recess in church

parts.note: re means on or concerning
an apse is a vaulted recess, usually at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: Someone falls back onto a large alcove in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip back into an earlier bad state, such as illness, is to regress.

clue.text: Thursday in March: a girl appears

indicators.note: in means the day's abbreviation is placed inside the other letters

explanation.surface: A girl turns up on a Thursday in March.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name stands for a girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: Too hurried, this unsuccessful contestant?

parts.note: also means too, as well
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A contestant who rushed too much and failed.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing the term names a runner that did not finish among the placed horses, hence any loser.

clue.text: Girl Ed harassed in aircraft without a sound?

indicators.note: harassed means troubled or disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Ed pesters a girl inside a silent plane.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aeroplane flies silently on air currents.

clue.text: Drunks are so smooth?

definitions.meaning: drunks are intoxicated, slang for which is lubricated
a mechanism that runs smoothly has been thoroughly lubricated

explanation.surface: Are drunken people suave?
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means thoroughly tipsy and also literally greased so it runs without friction.

clue.text: Billiard ball that's not spotted?

parts.note: in billiards one cue ball is plain and the other carries a black spot, so the unmarked one is named by its colour

explanation.surface: A billiard ball nobody noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: English billiards uses three balls: a red and two cue balls, one plain and one marked with spots; 'not spotted' looks like 'not seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The plain cue ball in billiards is named for its pale colour.

clue.text: They are for promoting a CID officer

parts.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant in the CID, the British police's Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: A group are in favour of giving a detective a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertisements exist to publicise and sell products.

clue.text: Binder, I hesitate to say, under a pound

indicators.note: in a down entry under means the hesitation comes below the other letters

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
um is the noise someone makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: A speaker hesitantly admits a folder costs less than a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of blank pages for holding photos or stamps is a kind of binder.

clue.text: Firmly established moped is for repair

indicators.note: something sent for repair is taken apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sturdy, well-founded moped is in for mending.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule forced on people is set in place with authority, i.e. firmly instituted.

clue.text: Dying remains end in three months

definitions.meaning: a glowing piece of coal left in a dying fire
the closing letters common to September, November and December

explanation.surface: A dying man's body is to be dealt with by the close of a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A smouldering coal fragment is what's left of a fire that is going out.

clue.text: E Sussex town, heading off Suffolk females?

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex, in southern England

explanation.surface: A southern English town sends its women off to the county of Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk looks like the English county, but it is a breed of sheep, so its females are sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is a breed of sheep, and the females of sheep have their own name.

clue.text: Iron Maiden pursued by an employee of The Times?

indicators.note: pursued by means followed by, so the last piece comes after

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden, an over without runs

explanation.surface: The heavy-metal band Iron Maiden being chased by a newspaper worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Maiden' reads as the rock band, but splits into PRESS and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist works for a newspaper such as The Times.
